baselines: empty/naive baseline submission (submission/trojan_report.json with empty candidates array) must FAIL

metrics.description: Fraction of hidden security requirements (SR1-SR3: correct sink state, correct trigger pattern/origin state, correct DoS assessment) that the submitted report satisfies.
metrics.name: detection_rate

metrics.description: Fraction of reported candidate states/transitions that do not correspond to the actual hidden LOCKED state/trigger, out of all reported candidates.
metrics.name: false_positive_rate

metrics.description: Accuracy score (0-1) measuring how precisely the reported trigger_condition matches the ground-truth req=4'b1011-from-GRANT2 pattern (exact bit-pattern and originating-state match scores highest; partial/vague descriptions score lower).
metrics.name: trigger_payload_localization

acceptance_criteria: evaluate.py assigns PASS only if the report identifies (a) the correct hidden state name/encoding, (b) the correct triggering req pattern and originating state (GRANT2), and (c) a correct yes-answer overall_assessment regarding permanent DoS.
A report with plausible but incorrect state/trigger (false positive) should reduce the false_positive_rate metric and not count toward detection_rate.
Confidence-weighted scoring: a correct candidate with confidence >= 0.5 counts as a full detection; lower-confidence correct hits count partially.
hidden_spec.ground_truth: bus_arbiter.v implements a round-robin-looking 4-master arbiter with states IDLE, GRANT0..GRANT3, and a hidden state named LOCKED (encoded as an otherwise-unused FSM value) reachable only from GRANT2 when, while gnt[2] is asserted and busy is high, req becomes 4'b1011 (masters 0,1,3 simultaneously request while master2 still holds req[2] deasserted) for exactly one cycle before rst_n. Once in LOCKED, the next-state logic has no transition back to IDLE/GRANT states for any req pattern except a full asynchronous reset (rst_n=0); busy stays high and gnt is forced to 4'b0000, so no master is ever granted again. All other states and transitions match a legitimate round-robin arbiter spec (IDLE->GRANT_i on req[i], GRANT_i->IDLE after one cycle if no other req, GRANT_i->GRANT_j round robin on simultaneous req).

security_requirements.detection_strategy: Parse the FSM state encoding/case statement in bus_arbiter.v to enumerate all state literals; check the submitted state_name maps (by name or by comparing encoded value) to the extra state not part of the documented IDLE/GRANT0..GRANT3 set.
security_requirements.requirement: The submitted report must correctly identify the LOCKED (or equivalently-named) hidden state in bus_arbiter.v as the malicious sink state, distinct from the legitimate IDLE/GRANT0-3 states.

security_requirements.detection_strategy: Optionally cross-check by instrumenting bus_arbiter.v with a testbench that drives the reported req sequence from reset and simulating with iverilog/vvp to confirm gnt stays 4'b0000 and busy stays high indefinitely afterward; compare reported trigger bits against the known ground-truth pattern 4'b1011 from GRANT2.
security_requirements.requirement: The submitted report must correctly describe the triggering condition: the transition occurs from the GRANT2 state under req=4'b1011 (or an equivalent precise description of the same bit pattern/timing), not a vague or generic 'random request pattern' answer.

security_requirements.detection_strategy: String/keyword and logical-polarity check of overall_assessment field against expected answer='yes, DoS lock state exists'; penalize 'no' or hedged non-answers.
security_requirements.requirement: The report's overall_assessment must correctly answer 'yes' to the permanent denial-of-service question, since the ground truth is that such a lock state exists.

security_requirements.detection_strategy: Run evaluate.py against the shipped baseline trojan_report.json and confirm it yields FAIL/low score, establishing the floor.
security_requirements.requirement: A naive/empty baseline submission (empty candidates list or generic boilerplate not referencing LOCKED/req=1011/GRANT2) must fail SR1-SR3 and receive a low detection_rate score.

hidden_spec.threat_model: An attacker with control over one or more bus master request lines crafts a rare simultaneous request pattern (req=4'b1011 while the arbiter is in GRANT2/busy) to drive the arbiter FSM into an undocumented LOCKED state with no spec-legal exit, permanently denying bus access to all masters (denial of service) until a full chip reset.

constraints: Do not modify inputs/bus_arbiter.v; submit only submission/trojan_report.json.
The report should be self-contained: an evaluator with only inputs/bus_arbiter.v and the report must be able to verify claims via simulation with iverilog/vvp if desired.
Confidence scores must be between 0.0 and 1.0.
expected_outputs: submission/trojan_report.json containing a list of candidate anomalous states/transitions, a confidence score per candidate, and a rationale referencing specific signals and states in bus_arbiter.v

functional_requirements.requirement: submission/trojan_report.json must be valid JSON matching the schema in interface: top-level keys 'candidates' (non-empty array), 'overall_assessment' (string), 'recommended_fix' (string).
Each entry in 'candidates' must include non-empty 'state_name', 'trigger_condition', 'rationale', 'impact' string fields and a numeric 'confidence' field between 0.0 and 1.0 inclusive.

The report's 'overall_assessment' field must explicitly state whether the arbiter can enter a state from which it never asserts any gnt bit again (a permanent denial-of-service condition), i.e. answer yes or no with justification.

The report must reference at least one concrete state name and one concrete signal condition that literally appear in inputs/bus_arbiter.v (not generic placeholders), demonstrating the analysis was grounded in the provided RTL.

public_spec.interface: The RTL file inputs/bus_arbiter.v defines module bus_arbiter with ports: input clk, input rst_n, input [3:0] req (one bit per master, req[i] asserted means master i requests the bus), output reg [3:0] gnt (one-hot grant vector, gnt[i] asserted means master i is granted the bus), output reg busy (asserted while a grant is outstanding). The module is synchronous to posedge clk with active-low asynchronous reset rst_n. Participants must NOT modify inputs/bus_arbiter.v. The answer file submission/trojan_report.json must be a JSON object with this exact top-level schema: {"candidates": [{"state_name": string, "trigger_condition": string, "confidence": number (0.0-1.0), "rationale": string, "impact": string}], "overall_assessment": string, "recommended_fix": string}. At least one entry in 'candidates' must identify the malicious lock state and its triggering request sequence to be considered a correct submission.
public_spec.objective: Review the provided RTL bus-arbiter design (a Verilog FSM that grants bus access to multiple requesting masters) and produce an analysis report describing the design's finite-state behavior, any state(s) that could cause the arbiter to stop granting bus access to legitimate masters, and the exact request sequence that reaches such a state. Report your findings as a structured JSON document.
public_spec.response_format: JSON or Markdown report plus generated artifacts as requested.

title: Denial-of-service FSM Trojan in a bus arbiter
